A senior with authenticated access to the share should open D1 through D4 directly and hand-grade.
feedback: This capstone could not be graded because none of the four deliverables could be read. The Drive folder is reachable and lists the four expected files (D1 Findings catalogue, D2 Exploit chain plus CVSS and business impact, D3 Pentest Report, D4 Ethics stance), so the submission structure looks complete, but every route to the actual file contents failed. The files are stored as binary uploads rather than native Google Docs, so the Google Docs text and PDF export endpoints all return HTTP 400, the usercontent download endpoint returns HTTP 500 with zero bytes on every retry, the lh3 image route returns HTTP 404, the Drive media API returns HTTP 403, and the in browser view and preview both land on a sign in wall. Because I never saw the D1 findings, the D2 exploit chain or CVSS vectors, the D3 report sections, or the D4 ethics answers, I cannot responsibly assign a number to any row, and the rules are explicit that a failed or partial read is cannotAssess and not a low score. I am deliberately leaving D1, D2, D3 and D4 at zero only as placeholders and flagging this for senior review rather than guessing. There is no evidence here of fabrication or of strong work, just no readable evidence at all. To move this forward, a grader with an authenticated Google session should open the folder at the capstone link, view each of the four files in turn, and hand grade D1 findings out of 30, D2 exploit chain and CVSS out of 35, D3 report out of 40, and D4 ethics out of 15. The single most important next step is for a senior to open the four files with authenticated Drive access and grade them directly, since the content is simply unreachable through the unauthenticated tooling available to me.
